nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the number of permutations $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that the number of cycles of $\sigma$ of length at least $2$ plus the number of fixed points of $\sigma$ equals $k$ is the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $c(n, k)$. In other words, $c(n, k)$ counts the permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles, each fixed point counted as a cycle of…
nodes.title: Stirling numbers of the first kind count permutations by cycles

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of a finite type, the number of cycles of $\sigma$, counting each fixed point as a cycle of length one, equals the number of cycles of $\sigma$ of length at least $2$ (the length of its cycle type) plus the number of fixed points of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Counting cycles via the cycle type

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of a finite type $\alpha$, the number of cycles of $\sigma$, counting each fixed point as a cycle of length one, is the number of equivalence classes of $\alpha$ under the relation that holds between $x$ and $y$ when $\sigma^i(x) = y$ for some integer $i$.
nodes.title: Number of cycles of a permutation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the signed Stirling number of the first kind is the integer $(-1)^{n-k} c(n,k)$, where $c(n,k)$ is the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind (the number of permutations of $n$ elements with exactly $k$ cycles) and $n - k$ is truncated subtraction, equal to $0$ when $k > n$.

nodes.summary: The rising factorial is the generating polynomial of the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind: `ascPochhammer S n = ∑_{k=0}^{n} stirlingFirst n k * X ^ k` (Graham–Knuth–Patashnik, §6.1).
